name: Harley Kelly
life: “I still remember offering a promise beside a sink that cost more than I thought.” On Tuesday, near Studio Boulevard, Harley waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I posted the job without asking the apprentice what I once said across a sink.
appearance: Harley has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for a loose dark braid. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Harley gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Harley carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To account for both candidates' prior labor.
family: Ava Nichols is Harley’s second cousin. Harley chooses the music. Ava puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The dead man's tab*, Ava says, “I made the soup. He said it tasted like school dinners, which I discovered was a compliment.”
connections: Harriet Ho. The shift manager has to cost the proposal that upends a simple hiring contest. Also in the story is Ida Boyd (apprentice).

reactions.situation: The new baker gets the first oven slot
reactions.response: Harley makes sure the other applicant gets a comparable chance with the same oven.
reactions.asWritten: The new baker gets the first oven slot. Harley makes sure the other applicant gets a comparable chance with the same oven.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Harley asks which other bill repayment would displace, then offers only what the household can afford to give.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Harley offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
